newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First to retain several key economic Acts.
newsitem.headline: NZ First to retain several key economic Acts.

text.p: New Zealand First Party leader Winston Peters said on Tuesday the new coalition government would retain the Reserve Bank Act, but widen the underlying inflation target band and add the goal of sustainable economic growth to the RBNZ's Policy Targets Agreement.
Peters also said the Employment Contracts Act would retained, with amendments. The Fiscal Responsibility Act would be retained in its current format.
Peters said NZ First had agreed on policy platforms with its National Party coalition partner.
"They include to retain the Reserve Bank Act but including the objective of sustainable economic growth in the Reserve Bank's Policy Target Agreement," Peters said.
The RBNZ's current zero to two percent annual underlying inflation target would embrace a zero to three percent target.
The coalition would run budget surpluses which would be dedicated to repaying debt and reducing net public debt to 17 percent of GDP by the year 2000.
Amendments to the Employment Contracts Act would cover fair bargaining and the minimum wage.
